method: python training/build_sequential.py --data-dir ml-32m training/benchmark_sequential.py found that the order of likes predicts what people love next (NDCG@10 0.127 vs 0.113 for item-kNN from the 3 most recent likes, 95% CI +0.010 to +0.018). "More like X" starts from one movie, so it gets its own test before anything ships. Rules written before running, on the same 1-in-5 sample, time split and 3,000 + 3,000 viewers as confirm_like.py: source = each viewer's most recent like; the score is (1 - a) x fans' closeness + a x "liked next"; a is picked on validation viewers, then compared once on test viewers with fans alone (what ships today). Only if it wins with a 95% interval above zero is the model built on all of MovieLens 32M (each movie's 100 most likely next movies, same movie index as the app) into data/seq_chain.npz. A second test, same rules, checks the main ranking (Top Picks, Tonight's Show) against the shipped fan ranking from each viewer's 3 most recent likes. Writes data/seq_like_confirm.json and data/seq_main_confirm.json either way; the model is built if either test passes.
